rawCandidates.selectionReason: Best restaurant-detail reference for menu tabs plus reservation sidebar, but food/photos/proof are not reusable.
Clear first-viewport decision bar for booking/search jobs; maps to menu/table/private enquiry routing.
Quick-search chips and account dropdown show multiple visitor jobs without burying the CTA.
Breakfast/availability row shows time-sensitive food decisions; useful with strong freshness gates.
Popular dishes plus menu tabs show how food proof can be structured, while invented dishes are banned.
Dark quote block is an anti-proof reference and a footer/nav contrast reference.
Browse-menu CTA and food scene composition are useful as a media discipline stress test.
Soft proof carousel can become source-backed process/menu freshness proof.
Large outcome-stat proof is useful mainly as an anti-reference for fake venue metrics.
Three-card quote grid and fine print help define what not to invent for a fixture restaurant.
Premium calm hero with artifact and legal strip supports a restrained menu-freshness notice pattern.
Centered business hero with alert bar gives a simple template for menu freshness and visitor-job routing.
Dark object-led product hero is a dramatic anti-reference for this food fixture unless remixed heavily.
Premium dark editorial CTA section useful as a supper-club mood reference but not for portraits/celebrity proof.
Resource page lead form and phone mockup suggest how private dinner enquiry can sit after primary menu CTA.
Food-photo-heavy restaurant detail is a precise anti-reference for unapproved dish images.
Split view-menu hero shows direct menu CTA and food media contrast.
Menu detail with last-updated note is central to menu freshness governance.
Marketplace restaurant menu structure shows category nav, cart state, and item grid patterns.
Delivery-storefront map/category/deal layout is a useful anti-reference for app-like clutter.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: The first viewport must separate menu browsing, table booking, and private dinner enquiry instead of forcing one generic CTA.
Use a visible visitor-job bar with menu, supper club, private table, and voucher paths.
Hero can be wide and quiet if the decision controls remain visible in the first fold.
Desktop horizontal decision bar should become four stacked thumb-friendly actions on mobile.

bannedUses: Do not copy OpenTable marketplace inventory, restaurant names, location detection, stars, reviews, or reservation availability.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Menu detail, reservation action, and gift/private enquiry can coexist if each has clear freshness/source status.
Primary view-menu CTA should stay separate from reserve/enquire actions so visitors do not misread availability.
Private-table enquiry needs a small request form, not a fake live booking widget.
Use Bath/Walcot only at area level and do not show hours, phone, or prices unless verified.

bannedUses: Do not copy photos, dish names, ratings, reviews, reservation slots, phone numbers, payment cards, or gift-card fulfillment claims.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: A split hero can reserve a media side for owner-supplied food photos; before approval use menu-board or receipt artifacts.
Use a pale dining-room base with one citrus or lantern accent for menu action, not a full food-app palette.
Flat paper/menu surfaces should replace glossy restaurant marketplace cards.
Keep menu panels crisp with slight rounding; avoid app-like pill overload.

bannedUses: Do not copy Sweetgreen brand, dish imagery, rewards/order account UI, late-order status, or order-again modules.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Menu sections need category tabs, item rows, short descriptions, source status, and a clear full-menu path.
Menu state needs fresh, stale, unavailable, and owner-review-required labels.
Menu tabs and reservation/enquiry controls require keyboard order, visible focus, and readable mobile text.
Visible menu categories should map to truthful structured data only when the menu is verified.

bannedUses: Do not copy dish names, prices, third-party menu provider marks, review counts, reservation slots, or last-updated dates.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use the proof area for source-backed facts: menu verified status, photo status, contact path, and fixture limitations.
Use one soft layered proof surface rather than nested card stacks.
Optional proof motion should be manual carousel or subtle reveal, never auto-rotating fake testimonials.
Replace testimonial drama with concise restaurant operations language: menu, table, private dinner, voucher.

bannedUses: Do not invent customer quotes, portraits, names, logos, review snippets, or satisfaction claims.

shortlist.structureFamily: centered business hero with alert bar

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use large confident sans headline with a warmer supporting type rhythm for menu sections.
Let the hero breathe, but keep the menu/action rail visible on desktop and early on mobile.
Use tiny functional symbols for menu, table, private enquiry, and voucher instead of decorative food icons.
Alert/freshness bar should disclose fixture or stale menu status rather than pretending today’s menu is verified.

bannedUses: Do not copy Pinterest trend claims, ad-platform messaging, business-account CTAs, or decorative social-commerce imagery.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Secondary path can lead from private dinner block into a short enquiry form after menu browsing.
Phone/menu mockups can become paper menu, table plan, or receipt graphics without fake food photos.
A static menu-board artifact avoids heavy photo galleries until real assets are supplied.
Define tokens for menu paper, lantern accent, reservation rail, stale/fresh labels, and action states.

bannedUses: Do not copy corporate wellness language, phone UI screenshots, lead-magnet claims, star reviews, or case-study language.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: A dense menu/catalog layout is useful only below the first decision point, with a calm owner-site wrapper.
Item cards need unavailable/photo-missing/source-missing states before they become customer-visible.
Cart patterns should become enquiry/reservation intent, not fake ordering.
Do not load a marketplace-style item grid unless actual menu data and photos are approved.

bannedUses: Do not copy DoorDash app shell, cart drawer, discounts, ratings, delivery distance, prices, item photos, or ordering functionality.

antiReferences.rejectionReason: Food-photo gallery would create fake dish and interior proof without owner-supplied media.
Giant stats would invent customer, booking, or popularity proof.
Delivery marketplace map/deal UI would turn a venue page into an app clone and imply unsupported ordering.
Celebrity portrait strip and dark premium mood overpower the small local supper-club job.

remixDirection.summary: A menu-first hybrid restaurant page: first-fold visitor-job selector, no-photo menu-board artifact, clear cafe/supper/private paths, source/freshness status, and a restrained reservation/enquiry rail.
selectedMoves: OpenTable reservation decision bar remixed into menu/table/private/voucher routing without marketplace proof.
Sweetgreen split menu hero remixed as a no-photo menu-board and paper receipt system.
OpenTable menu freshness detail converted into explicit source/freshness governance.
Assembly proof surface converted into source-backed menu/contact/photo status, not testimonials.
ClassPass resource/form pattern adapted into private dinner enquiry below the menu decision.
explicitRejects: No stock food photos, invented dish photos, fake interiors, guests, chefs, reviews, ratings, prices, opening hours, delivery promises, or reservation availability.
No marketplace cart, delivery app shell, SaaS dashboard proof, logo strips, celebrity imagery, or copied brand colors.
No exact layout copy from Mobbin; use only ingredient-level structure, state, and hierarchy lessons.
